correctness.rationale: D:f↦(f(n+1)-f(n)) is onto isometry from real Lip_0(Z) to two-sided bounded sequences and intertwines all integer translations with bilateral shift. On an invariant real plane the restricted bilateral shift is invertible isometry, so eigenvalues lie on unit circle and there are no Jordan blocks. Each complex shift eigenspace in scalar bounded sequences is at most 1-dimensional. Thus either eigenpair +1/-1 gives square norm |a|+|b|, or conjugate e^{±i theta} gives sup_n |a cos(n theta)+b sin(n theta)|; rational frequencies give regular even N polygon, irrational dense orbits give Euclidean. Finite-dimensional subspaces are pointwise closed and polar duality yields same predual isometry list. For arbitrary centered ellipse E⊂regular polygon K⊂tE, isotropic facet normals and vertices plus tr(Q) tr(Q^-1)>=4 yield t>=sec(pi/N), matching circular ellipse. Normal-gap estimates prove coefficient norms and Banach–Mazur distances have exactly rational-frequency discontinuities. Independently computed the polygonal support minimum for ten rational angles q=3,...,21 and matched cos(pi/N), corroborating without replacing infinite proof.
